sources.entry: AWStats - Generate statistics from web, streaming, ftp or mail server logfiles. (Demo, Source Code) GPL-3.0 Perl

summary.one_liner: AWStats is a long-running Perl log analyzer that turns web, streaming, FTP and mail server logs into visitor, page, and error statistics, runnable from the command line or as a CGI.
summary.what_it_does: AWStats parses server logfiles (IIS, Apache, and other web, wap, proxy, streaming, FTP or mail logs) and reports visits, unique visitors, pages, hits, bandwidth, hours and days of week, and visitor domains or countries. It also covers browsers, operating systems, robots, search engines and keyphrases, entry, exit and most-viewed pages, file types, and HTTP errors with referers. It runs from the command line for static reports or as a CGI for dynamic, on-demand updates with filters. Output is static HTML/XHTML (single or framed), with experimental PDF export and XML database storage for XSLT processing. The README says it needs only the Perl Encode module and that it has a Webmin module and CSS-customizable output.
use_cases: analyze apache or iis web server logs
count unique visitors and page hits from logs
find broken links and 404 errors in logs
see which search keywords brought visitors
monitor bot and robot traffic on a site
produce static html statistics pages from logfiles
how_to_run: Ensure your server writes web access logs to a readable file
Ensure Perl is installed and the Encode module is available
Copy wwwroot/cgi-bin/awstats.model.conf and edit it as your single configuration file
Run wwwroot/cgi-bin/awstats.pl from the command line against your config to build statistics
Or deploy wwwroot/cgi-bin/awstats.pl as a CGI script to view statistics in a browser
See the docs/ directory for full installation and setup documentation
notable: Analyzes many log types beyond web servers, including streaming, FTP and mail logs
Runs both as a command-line batch tool and as a CGI with on-demand updates
Single configuration file to edit, with plugins and filters
Includes a Webmin module and XML database output for XSLT processing
Reverse DNS lookup and country detection from IP or domain name
caveats: The README says the project is deprecated (November 2025) and no longer actively developed; it recommends migrating to Matomo Log Analytics
Dynamic CGI use requires a web server able to run CGI scripts
keywords: see who visits my site from logs
